name: European Central Bank (ECB)
summary: ECB, Day 246. The ECB held its deposit rate at 2.50% on 29 Oct after debating a hike, and Lagarde signalled — conditionally — that December is the next step if the energy shock is confirmed; Reuters' sources call a 17 Dec hike 'all but certain', followed by a pause. Energy inflation is near 19% and TTF crossed €100 the day before, but the bank also noted that the bond-yield rise has tightened financing and France is in recession. In the same hour Lagarde announced she will leave early, on 7 Feb 2027. The war reaches the ECB through gas and oil prices; the constraint is French debt.

recent_signals.headline: **29 OCT: UNANIMOUS HOLD AT 2.50% AFTER DEBATING A HIKE; DECEMBER CONDITIONALLY SIGNALLED; LAGARDE LEAVING EARLY.** DFR 2.50% / MRO 2.65% / MLF 2.90%. Lagarde: the Council discussed whether 'a rate rise would be appropriate, but decided unanimously to keep rates on hold'; if the situation 'is going to be confirmed… the sense of direction is quite clear'. Statement: energy prices 'have risen above the baseline' and 'have continued to rise, posing upside risks'; energy inflation 18.9% (Sept), headline 3.8%; 'financing conditions have tightened'; on France the solution 'lies at home'. Reuters sources: a 17 Dec hike 'all but certain', then a pause; staff estimates show the yield rise cutting 2027–28 growth by 100bp and inflation by 90bp. Lagarde will step down on 7 Feb 2027 ('I don't think that I can be comfortable in that neutrality'). Euro-area flash HICP due 4 Nov; Q3 GDP +0.4% q/q (France −0.1%). (CONFIRMED decision; REPORTED sources; intel ISR-A9/A10/B1, MAC-A16)

29 Oct: a hold at DFR 2.50% is ~97% priced; December hike consensus ('a done deal' — Nomura; ING: 'the bond market has taken over the ECB's job'). Euro-area October flash HICP is 4 Nov (not 30 Oct) — the ECB meets without it; September HICP final 3.8%. France is the bigger story: OAT >5%, spread ~150–170bp, riots. Schnabel's early exit reshapes the debate. TTF €97 intraday feeds the December case. (REPORTED pricing; intel ISR-A10/B3)

recent_signals.headline: **THE ECB MEETS THURSDAY 23 JULY into a gas shock its own projections do not capture.** Markets price ~95.3% hold (3.4% for +25bp). This is a NON-PROJECTION meeting, so June's staff forecasts stand unrevised — and those put 2026 headline inflation at 3.0% with **Q3 energy inflation at 12.5%, a forecast made BEFORE TTF broke EUR57.** The ECB hiked 25bp on 11 June (deposit rate 2.25%, MRO 2.40%, MLF 2.65%, effective 17 Jun) — its first hike in three years, explicitly attributed to the energy path. CNBC's European desk reports an ECB rates rethink amid an 'extremely volatile' outlook. The physical backdrop is worse than the price: EU gas storage 53% full against a 75% five-year norm (lowest in 15 years), July injections at a six-year low, net injections since April covering only 40% of winter need, and **Brussels has already RELAXED the mandatory storage target from 90% to 80% with a further 4% deviation allowed — a regulator conceding the target is unreachable before winter begins.** Germany has passed a two-month, EUR1.6bn fuel-tax relief with petrol above the symbolic EUR2/litre — the political tell that this has stopped being a market story there. CONFIRMED.

**The ECB will HOLD Thursday 23 July, with September flagged as the 'reckoning.'** Eurozone CPI is 2.8% (20 Jul); this is a NON-projection meeting, so June's stale Q3 energy-inflation forecast (12.5%, set before TTF broke EUR57) stands unrevised while **TTF is now EUR61.37 (+44.8% 1M, a new cycle high)** on the continued absence of Qatari LNG through Hormuz. Like the Fed, the ECB is treating a genuine supply shock as deferrable — the September meeting, with fresh projections, is where the energy path bites. CONFIRMED.

**The ECB PAUSED on 23 July, explicitly citing Middle East/oil risk — the stagflation frame now has central-bank confirmation.** Reuters: 'ECB to pause rate hikes but may signal more is needed'; Anadolu: 'remains cautious amid Middle East risks'; France 24: 'New Mideast fighting puts eurozone rate-setters on alert.' Eurozone CPI 2.8%; a non-projection meeting, so June's stale Q3 energy-inflation forecast (12.5%) stands unrevised while TTF prints a fresh cycle high (EUR63.75). **September is flagged as the decision point, and the debate is a HIKE not a cut** — i.e. the ECB is deferring the energy shock to Q3 exactly as the Fed is. This confirms the 'September reckoning' the graph flagged. CONFIRMED (decision landing just after the data window; well-corroborated).
